_meta.description: GPU catalog for the VRAM/throughput planner — capacity, bandwidth, dense BF16 compute, and 3-tier hourly pricing. Keyed by slug (t4-16, a100-80, ...), the same convention benchmarks/data.json's GPU half of each key uses. index.html's GPU_TABLE and generate_report.py's GPUS are generated from this file by tools/sync_data.py, between 'GPU_TABLE:BEGIN'/'GPU_TABLE:END' marker comments in each — edit this file, then re-run that script; do not hand-edit the generated blocks. The row schema carries what both engines read plus the structural fields the v1.1 work needs (vendor, perfKey, devices, form, caps). It is designed to grow — a vendor tag, a per-board device count, a fabric/interconnect tier are all expected to land on this same table in later commits — so a new column is the likely shape of that change, not a new table.

schema.gb: VRAM per card, in GiB. Matches the manufacturer's marketing number, which is already GiB in practice — nvidia-smi reports an '80 GB' H100 as 79.6 GiB, not 80/1e9*2^30 worth of decimal GB.
schema.bw: Memory bandwidth in GB/s, used as the decode roofline's bandwidth term.
schema.hyper: Hyperscaler on-demand price in $/hr per GPU (AWS/GCP/Azure).
schema.spec: Specialized-cloud price in $/hr per GPU (Lambda, CoreWeave, RunPod and similar).
schema.spot: Spot/marketplace price in $/hr per GPU (Vast.ai and similar).
schema.tflops: Dense BF16 tensor-core TFLOPS. NVIDIA datasheets headline the 2:4-structured-sparsity number (e.g. H100 SXM '1,979 teraFLOPS* / *With sparsity'); LLM inference does not use structured sparsity, so this is the dense figure — half the headline number.
schema.name: Display name shown in the GPU dropdown's option label and in generate_report.py's PDF/CLI output, e.g. 'H100 80 GB'.
schema.vendor: The hardware vendor, 'nvidia' on every row here. Carried onto each engine's state but read by neither engine's arithmetic: it used to select the PERF constants, and that is perfKey's job now, because one vendor spans architectures whose measured constants differ. Kept for vendor-specific deployment guidance, which is a different question from how fast a card is.
schema.perfKey: Which entry of each engine's PERF table (memory-bandwidth utilisation, decode/prefill MFU, observed band) this card's throughput and TTFT are computed with. 'nvidia' on every row here. Named for a set of measured constants, not for a vendor, so rows share an entry only when the same measurements apply to them. A perfKey with no PERF entry is a supported state, not an error: the card still gets its full VRAM breakdown, fit verdict, cost and vLLM command, while every throughput and TTFT figure is absent (null, never 0) and each view says that no measured utilisation is published for it. Neither engine falls back to another entry's constants. Required on every row — tools/sync_data.py refuses a row without it — so an omission cannot quietly select anything.
schema.devices: How many independent accelerator devices one board presents to the runtime. 1 for every card here. Multi-GCD boards — MI250X is one OAM containing two GCDs — are one catalog row with devices:2, because that is how they are bought and priced, and the engine multiplies rather than the catalog duplicating a row.
schema.form: Board form factor: 'sxm', 'pcie' or 'consumer'. Read today as the NVLink gate — only sxm boards here carry it — and the prerequisite for the fabric/domain tier a later commit adds.
schema.caps: Architecture-determined capability flags. caps.fp8 is FP8 tensor-core support: false on Turing (T4) and Ampere (A100), true from Ada and Hopper on.
schema.default: Present and true on exactly one row: the card the tool selects when nothing else is specified. Derived by both engines instead of each hardcoding a slug.
schema.priceSource: Provenance for hyper/spec/spot, written by tools/price_check.py — not read by index.html or generate_report.py, so it never reaches the generated GPU_TABLE blocks and carries no runtime cost. Optional object keyed by tier name ('hyper'/'spec'/'spot'); a tier key is present only once that tier's price has been confirmed against a live source, as { provider, sku, region, date }: provider is the source ('azure'/'aws'/'lambda'/'coreweave'/'vast'), sku is that provider's own SKU/instance-type/meter/plan name (verbatim, e.g. 'Standard_ND96isr_H100_v5'), region is the provider's region ('eastus') or 'global' for sources with no regional pricing, and date ('YYYY-MM-DD', UTC) is when it was read. A tier missing from priceSource — or the whole key absent, true of every row today — means no automated provenance is recorded: either the price predates this tracking (all twelve rows do; their original sourcing is not reliably known, see tmp/research/price-sources.md's own UNVERIFIED section, and is not guessed at here) or no automatable source exists for that tier (tools/price_check.py's SOURCE_MAP says which, and why, per slug). Absence is not an error, and the tool never invents a value to fill it.
